Name: Carbon Continuum
Description:
We make carbon nanotubes from industrial carbon emissions. Yup, the kind of carbon emissions spewing from factories that's linked to global warming, or more accurately, climate change. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are the material of the future. Similar to carbon microfiber, this material is orders of magnitude stronger and more light-weight than aluminum. Applications for such properties are abundant and limitless; for example, sporting goods, construction, electronics and all modes of transportation, particularly for space travel. Since we are using waste carbon emissions (mainly methane, which is 20x more potent in global warming effects than CO2), we can offer low-cost CNTs, enabling the use of this material on a commercial scale. 

Our technology work likes this: First, we analyze that composition of the waste gas, and then affix a customized reactor to convert the gas into nanomaterials. Our reactors are uniquely designed to facilitate a chemical reaction promoting the growth of CNTs and other nanomaterials. 

Currently, we are honing in on methane as the primary source to make multi-walled CNTs and sending samples for quality analysis and application R&D. We are aiming to secure funding to build a larger reactor to increase production capacity.

Name: Quantum Synthetics
Description:
Quantum Synthetics is an open-access digital repository and collaborative network built to bridge the gap between abstract physics equations and Advanced Material Engineering. Historically, discovering physical materials required decades of expensive wet-lab trial and error. 
Today, the convergence of quantum mechanics and computer-driven modeling shrinks that timeline to weeks. 
Quantum Synthetics serves as a high-value visual mapping of how raw mathematical formulas translate into real-world, scalable technologies. We focus our curation exclusively on Four pillars reshaping deep-tech research those are: Computational Chemistry, Quantum Mechanics, Advanced Nanomaterials Tracking and Advanced Instrumentation Awareness 
Who belongs here?
This ecosystem is built for University Science students bridging textbooks with industry, independent researchers seeking a collaborative network, and deep-tech enthusiasts fascinated by microscopic engineering. Driving a global scientific conversation does not require a multi-million dollar corporate laboratory. It simply requires a shared obsession with precision at the atomic scale.

Name: Pharmaceutical Innovation and Translational Research Lab (PITRL)
Description:
At the Pharmaceutical Innovation and Translational Research Laboratory (PITRL), Department of Pharmaceutics, NIPER Hyderabad, we are committed to advancing next-generation therapeutic strategies for the prevention, management, and treatment of complex diseases. Our multidisciplinary research focuses on a diverse range of health challenges and unmet clinical needs, including cancer (breast, prostate, oral, lung, brain, and skin cancers), diabetes and its ocular complications, diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), neurodegenerative disorders, and dermal conditions such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and melanoma.
To address these challenges, we ideate, design, and establish innovative nanocarrier-based drug delivery systems, including lipid nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles, metallic and inorganic nanoparticles, and electrospun nanofibers, that enhance therapeutic efficacy, target specificity, and patient compliance.
Beyond nanoparticle platforms, PITRL also pioneers the development of advanced biomaterials, including stimuli-responsive gels and polymeric films, engineered for controlled release, regenerative applications, and personalized treatment approaches.
Our overarching goal is to translate laboratory innovations into clinically viable solutions, bridging the gap between pharmaceutical research and real-world therapy to improve global healthcare outcomes.

Principal Investigator (PI): Prof. (Dr.) Saurabh Srivastava, Ph.D. FTASc.

Our research aims to combine theoretical modeling, photonic system design, and computational techniques to develop robust quantum-enabled technologies which find their applications in the field of communication, sensing, and computation.

With support from national agencies like DST-TSDP, the center is currently executing projects worth over ₹1.2 crore in low-cost healthcare diagnostics. Modern environments are characterized by increasing informational and sensory noise. Nanophotonic Gating: Leveraging SAW-modulated Holographic Polymer-Dispersed Liquid Crystals (H-PDLC) to create a "Silk Path" of foveal clarity while diffracting peripheral visual noise at the molecular level.

Skeletal Audio Suppression: Integrating Active Bone-Conduction Suppression to neutralize structural background noise, maintaining the integrity of the natural ear canal for essential communication.

Neural Hub Integration: A low-latency synchronization engine that aligns visual and auditory gating to ensure biological comfort and prevent vestibular mismatch.

Mission: Sensory Sovereignty
